mainEntity.name: Do secondary dwelling units require separate plumbing and electrical systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, existing residential plumbing and electrical systems must frequently be upgraded or expanded to support an independent dwelling unit. Adding a complete bathroom with a walk-in shower, a water heater, and a dedicated kitchen with cooking appliances significantly increases utility loads. Detached units require dedicated subpanels and trenching for supply and sewer lines connected back to the main house or municipal ties. During project planning, Bay City Remodeling & Bathrooms assesses your current breaker capacity and plumbing lines to determine the necessary upgrades.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, units require dedicated plumbing lines and expanded electrical capacity, often involving new subpanels, trenching, and independent water heater installations.
